__README__: Migrations merged BEFORE scripts/migration-lint.mjs existed, with a written reason each.
RECORDED, not suppressed — and the difference is executable. `pnpm lint:migrations` PRINTS
every entry below as a NOTICE on each run, so an exempt finding is visible in the same output
as a failing one; it just does not fail the build. A NEW migration cannot join this list
without an owner editing this file, which is the point: the cost of an exception is a visible
diff, not silence. Two tests keep it honest — every entry must name a real migration and rule
with a checkable reason, and none may be DEAD.
EVERY ENTRY IS KEYED PER SITE — "<RULE>:<line>", where a site is ONE SQL query as PostgreSQL's
grammar sees it. Keying by rule alone would let one accepted site discharge every other
finding of that rule in the same file — the ledger committing the very defect the rule
detects. An entry must match the finding's rule AND its line exactly.
That granularity is the correction PR #423 was closed for failing to make twice: its evidence
was gathered per FILE and then per BLOCK, so one correct guard discharged the requirement for
every defective neighbour beside it.
ONE OF THE TWO ENTRIES IS A LIVE DEFECT on an already-merged file. apps/api/prisma/** is
read-only to this unit, so it is REPORTED, not repaired; it needs its own unit.
A SECOND LIVE DEFECT — 20270920000000_decision_option_kinds:273 — has NO entry here and NO
backstop in this unit. It is detected only by MI-003, which is deferred at 08835700 on the
closed claude/migration-invariant-linter branch. An exemption for a rule that does not run
would suppress nothing and the no-dead-exemption test would refuse it. Deferring the rule did
not unfind the defect; it removed the alarm. See docs/MIGRATION_INVARIANTS.md.

20270225000000_phase4_t3_correction3.MI-001:167: LIVE DEFECT — REPORTED, NOT FIXED. Line 167 verifies the prerequisite composite foreign keys by conname + conrelid + contype='f' + convalidated, and never reads pg_trigger.tgenabled on tgconstraint. This is exactly the a222e91 (PR #411) class: `ALTER TABLE ... DISABLE TRIGGER ALL` leaves every column that guard reads unchanged while the keys stop enforcing, so a restored database with NO containment satisfies the prerequisite and is baselined as correct. apps/api/prisma/** is read-only to this unit, so this is recorded and reported rather than repaired here.

20270930000000_schedule_dependency_graph.MI-001:797: ACCEPTED — 1 site. Section 1e' (line 797) compares each foreign key's TARGET by confrelid OID and asks nothing about enforcement, which is what MI-001 reports. It is accepted on the merged evidence that section 1e'' — the next statement inside the SAME DO block, over the SAME five keys — asks the enforcement question per internal trigger and refuses tgenabled outside ('O','A'). The rule does not read that neighbour on 1e''s behalf, and it must not: that is precisely the coarser-than-the-site evidence PR #423 was closed for. The judgement that the neighbour covers this site is a human one, so it is written down here where a reviewer sees it.
